card.name: Auxiliary verbs in old scholarly prose
card.fires_on: Small helper words (he, was, been, had, be, those) right after a relative clause or 'have/has/may' in 19th-century style scholarly text. The next word is usually a past participle like felt, made, or suggested.

modes.label: Relative clause helper
modes.description: A pronoun or verb right after 'which' in a clause about feelings or hatred.
modes.example: testifies the warm affection which<< he>> had felt for him

modes.label: Perfect passive helper
modes.description: 'been' after 'have' or 'has' before a participle about theories or conjectures.
